summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1: 7.787), is carried by RCC cells in single-cell data (0.976 of tissue transcripts), and has a clinical-stage antibody (girentuximab, PHASE_3). It stays in the convergence top 10 in 0.894 of random re-weightings. It is not prognostic in TCGA (Cox padj 0.933) and is not a DepMap dependency, so it is a targeting and imaging handle rather than a functional vulnerability.

CD70 is the second surface-antigen target where all three knowledge sources agree: tumour-up RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), TCGA-KIRC replication (log2FC 7.09), a purity-1 log2FC of 4.278, literature describing high and specific ccRCC expression as a downstream HIF target, and clinical-stage antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2, vorsetuzumab mafodotin PHASE_1). Like CA9, its case rests on tumour-selective surface expression, not on dependency.

NNMT is the strongest dual candidate. It is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709), tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), prognostic in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479) and supported by literature as a prognostic biomarker and potential target. It is rank 2 of the biomarker profile with p_top10 0.973. It is cytoplasmic and has no clinical drug, so the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

Most of the remaining convergence top 25 are proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR, PSAT1, ALDH6A1). Several are prognostic in TCGA and are best read as biomarkers of lost tubule identity, not as targets. The established drivers VHL and PBRM1 are mechanism, and the actionable route is downstream HIF-2alpha (EPAS1, belzutifan at APPROVAL), whose single-cell signal in this dataset is mainly endothelial. No omics-convergent target shows a selective DepMap dependency.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-vs-normal omics separate two groups. Up-regulated, tumour-intrinsic genes (CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3, NNMT, HK2) are up at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and stay up at purity 1. They fit the hypoxia- and glycolysis-driven state that follows VHL loss. Down-regulated genes (PSAT1, ALDH6A1, SLC22A8, ALDOB) mark loss of normal tubule identity and are prognostic.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.399, protein log2FC -1.925), sits on a frequently lost region (CNV loss frequency 0.355) with a positive copy-number-to-expression correlation (cis rho 0.525), and lower expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR -0.554). The copy-number link makes it one of the few biomarkers with a plausible genomic cause for its loss.

PBRM1 is recurrently mutated (frequency 0.362, 185 of 511 tumours) and sits on 3p, which is lost in 0.8 of tumours. It explains the 3p-loss driver mechanism rather than acting as an expression-level target.

literature.text: Literature and data converge most clearly for CA9, CD70 and NNMT (tumour-up targets) and for ALDOB and SLC22A8 (tumour-loss prognostic biomarkers). Most gene-level claims rest on one or two recent, often bioinformatic papers. SCARB1 and PIGR have no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus, and FABP1's relations concern colorectal cancer, so their ranks are data-driven.

MT1G is the clearest disagreement in the literature. One study reports it as a down-regulated negative regulator of ferroptosis, another reports that high MT1G drives growth and metastasis through CPT1B inhibition. The omics show MT1G down in tumour with a worse-prognosis direction when high (Cox padj 0.00201), which fits 'low in tumour, high is worse', but the tumour-suppressor versus oncogenic reading is unresolved.

ABAT is under-expressed in KIRC and prognostic (TCGA Cox padj 0.000347), and overexpression suppresses tumour growth via cGAS-STING in non-ccRCC models. The available drug (vigabatrin) inhibits ABAT, which would be counter-productive for a lost, tumour-suppressive gene, so ABAT is mechanism and biomarker, not a target.

external.text: EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target: belzutifan is at APPROVAL and its Open Targets association score is 0.4871. It is the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061, not significant at 0.05). It ranks only 38 in convergence because its RNA is mildly changed while the drug acts on the protein. This is the main disagreement between expression-driven convergence and clinical reality.

Open Targets, UniProt and DepMap split the tumour-up candidates by modality. CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are membrane proteins with antibody, ADC or radioligand programmes (girentuximab PHASE_3, cusatuzumab PHASE_2, AGS-16C3F PHASE_2). NNMT, SLC16A3 and SCARB1 have no clinical drug. None of them is a DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so tractability rests on surface accessibility, not on tumour dependency. MTOR, an established target, is not singled out by omics convergence.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic at single-cell resolution: RCC cells carry 0.976 of tissue transcripts, and, paired by donor, CA9 is higher in tumour cells than in proximal tubule (log2FC 7.739, padj 0.0189, 6 donors).

Several familiar ccRCC targets are not tumour-cell genes in this dataset. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of tumour transcripts), CD74 is held by macrophages and cDC, CXCR4 by T cells, and EPAS1 transcripts are mostly endothelial and fibroblast, with only a 0.051 share in RCC cells. MET and EGFR are mainly in RCC cells (0.935 and 0.948 of transcripts). The bulk immune signals FCGR3A and FCER1G are infiltration-driven and should not be read as tumour targets.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are surrounded by RCC (log2 enrichment 0.377, padj 0.00173), with an RCC composition-corrected share of 0.998 and only small macrophage neighbour enrichment (0.084). CA9 marks the tumour compartment in situ, consistent with its single-cell and purity profile.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) scores rank candidate sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (pLDDT 90.3, volume 126.8 A3, 1 accessible lysine) with ligand-site recall of 0.5, which makes it a modest site.

KDR has a higher-ranked site (0.841, pocket 361.1 A3, 7 accessible lysines), but its target cell is endothelial, so a degrader would act on the vasculature, not on tumour cells. CD70 has no structural analysis available.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the leading under-studied, undrugged candidate. RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts, it is higher in tumour cells than in proximal tubule (log2FC 5.366, padj 0.0193), its vital-organ expression is low (maximum nTPM 3, heart muscle) and it has no clinical drug. Its AlphaFold model is poor (pLDDT 58.91) with no usable pocket, so an antibody is the realistic modality.

RAB42 is the second tumour-track candidate. RCC holds 0.627 of its tumour transcripts, it has 2 ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and its AlphaFold model is confident (mean pLDDT 85.31) with a small best site (MGD score 0.5348, volume 37.4 A3) whose ligand-site validity was not checked.

In the immune track, LRRC25 (macrophage, no ccRCC papers, off-tumour bone marrow expression) and GAL3ST4 (macrophage, antibody-tractable) stand out. In the stroma track, HMCN1 (endothelium) and OLFML2A (fibroblasts) are weaker. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses with no dependency or functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.

validation.text: External replication and the purity check strengthen the tumour-up targets. CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and HK2 all replicate in TCGA-KIRC and keep their fold change at purity 1, so their bulk signal is not infiltration. In contrast, FCGR3A and FCER1G are weakened: their bulk increase follows immune infiltration. Prognosis strengthens NNMT and the tubule-loss biomarkers (PSAT1, ALDH6A1, PCK1, SLC6A19, ALDOB, SLC22A8) but not CA9, CD70 or SCARB1.

Somatic driver status points elsewhere. VHL is mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483) and PBRM1 is the second driver, but neither is an expression-level target. Its expression change is modest (RNA log2FC -0.479), so these drivers act through loss of function and the HIF-2alpha axis.

Selective DepMap dependency weakens every omics-convergent target: CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3 and SCARB1 show no ccRCC dependency. EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective signal, and it is borderline. No protein-adjusted kinase activity signal supports any top candidate, because none of them is a kinase.

robustness.text: Under 1000 random re-weightings, the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay in the target top 10 robustly, and SCARB1 and CA9 have the narrowest intervals. In the biomarker profile only PSAT1, NNMT and ALDH6A1 are robust. ALDOB and SLC22A8 are high on average but have wide biomarker intervals, and VHL's overall rank swings widely because it scores only on genetics. CA9 is the only gene robustly in the overall convergence top 10.

SCARB1 is the most weight-robust target-profile call (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1 to 8), even though it has no ccRCC literature in the corpus and no clinical drug. Its position rests on tumour-intrinsic up-regulation (purity-1 log2FC 3.762) and an Open Targets genetic association (0.519), not on knowledge-driven streams.

integration.text: Read together, the layers separate three groups. First, targets where omics, literature, external knowledge and cell context all converge: CA9 and CD70, both tumour-intrinsic surface antigens with clinical antibodies. Second, data-strong targets with little prior knowledge: NNMT (also prognostic), SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and HK2. Third, biomarkers of tubule-identity loss: PSAT1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC22A8 and PCK1. The disagreements are informative. EPAS1 is clinically validated but ranks low on expression and is stromal in single-cell data, and the absence of DepMap dependency for the convergent targets means they suit antigen-directed modalities better than inhibitors.

targets.rationale: Ranks 1 in convergence and 2 in the target profile (p_top10 0.939). It is tumour-up at RNA, protein and in TCGA-KIRC, carried by RCC cells (0.976 of transcripts), RCC-surrounded in situ, and targeted by girentuximab (PHASE_3). Not prognostic and not a dependency, so it is best used as an antibody, radioligand or imaging target.

Placed above SCARB1 despite a lower target score because literature and clinical programmes converge on it.

limitations.text: All omics are bulk tumour-vs-normal comparisons. The ranking is associative, not causal, and protein fold changes are compressed by TMT ratios.
No omics-convergent target shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so the targets are supported for antigen-directed modalities, not as functional vulnerabilities.

The literature corpus is small (about 320 ccRCC abstracts), and most gene-level claims rest on one or two, often bioinformatic, studies. The literature agent could inspect only the top 12 ranking rows.
Single-cell context comes from one cohort of 12 donors, with small proximal-tubule groups. Cell-type tables were not pulled for CD70 or NNMT.
MGD scores rank structural sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. Ligand-site validation was available only for CA9.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency or functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.
STRING interactions were not queried, and CA9's DepMap values had no citable evidence id beyond the ranking row.
